# SECTION 1.2 EXPONENTS AND SCIENTIFIC NOTATION

Solution Use the quotient rule to simplify each expression.

a. $\frac{(-2)^5}{(-2)^3} = (-2)^{5-3} = (-2)^2$

b. $\frac{t^6}{t^3} = t^{3-3} = t^0$

## Try it #2

Write each of the following products with a single base. Do not simplify further.

a. $\frac{z^5}{z^2}$ 
b. $\frac{(-3)^5}{-3}$

## Using the Power Rule of Exponents

Suppose an exponential expression is raised to some power. Can we simplify the result? Yes. To do this, we use the power rule of exponents. Consider the expression $(x^7)^3$. The expression inside the parentheses is multiplied three times because it has an exponent of 3. Then the result is multiplied three times because the entire expression has an exponent of 2.

$$\begin{align}
(x^7)^3 &= (x^7) \cdot (x^7) \cdot (x^7)\\
&= \underbrace{\left(\frac{7 \text{ factors}}{x \cdot x}\right) \cdot \left(\frac{7 \text{ factors}}{x \cdot x}\right) \cdot \left(\frac{7 \text{ factors}}{x \cdot x}\right)}_{}\\
&= x^{7 \cdot 3}\\
&= x^{21}
\end{align}$$

The exponent of the answer is the product of the exponents: $(x^7)^3 = x^{7 \cdot 3} = x^{21}$. In other words, when raising an exponential expression to a power, we write the result with the common base and the product of the exponents.

Be careful to distinguish between uses of the product rule and the power rule. When using the product rule, different terms with the same base are raised to exponents. In this case, you add the exponents. When using the power rule, a term in exponential notation is raised to a power. In this case, you multiply the exponents.

| Product Rule | Power Rule |
|---|---|
| $5^1 \cdot 5^4 = 5^{1+4} = 5^5$ | but | $(5^1)^4 = 5^{1 \cdot 4} = 5^4$ |
| $x^3 \cdot x^2 = x^{3+2} = x^5$ | but | $(x^3)^2 = x^{3 \cdot 2} = x^6$ |
| $(3a)^2(3a)^8 = (3a)^{2+8} = (3a)^{10}$ | but | $((3a)^2)^8 = (3a)^{2 \cdot 8} = (3a)^{16}$ |

### the power rule of exponents

For any real number $a$ and positive integers $m$ and $n$, the power rule of exponents states that

$$(a^m)^n = a^{m \cdot n}$$

## Example 3 Using the Power Rule

Write each of the following products with a single base. Do not simplify further.

a. $(x^7)^3$ 
b. $((2y)^3)^3$ 
c. $((-3)^4)^3$

Solution Use the power rule to simplify each expression.

a. $(x^7)^3 = x^{7 \cdot 3} = x^{21}$

b. $((2y)^3)^3 = (2y)^{3 \cdot 3} = (2y)^9$

c. $((-3)^4)^3 = (-3)^{4 \cdot 3} = (-3)^{12}$
